formationLabel: Lithuanian parish effort documented in 1896 · St. Joseph formally organized January 9, 1915 · suppressed and merged into St. Henry April 1, 1970
currentUse: The former St. Joseph church at 2123 Park Avenue, at MacKay Place, was standing in a geolocated 2023 photograph and described there as rehabilitated for residential use. The exterior is documented; present occupancy and interior or structural condition remain unverified. Sacramental records are held by the Archdiocese of St. Louis Archives.
summary: St. Joseph was St. Louis's Lithuanian Roman Catholic national parish. A Lithuanian parish fundraiser was documented in 1896, but the St. Joseph institution was formally organized on January 9, 1915. It acquired the former Protestant Church of Unity in 1916, celebrated its first Mass there on August 13, and had the church blessed on September 10. St. Joseph was suppressed and merged into St. Henry on April 1, 1970. Its Park Avenue church survives in converted use, while the archdiocesan location wording conflicts with the address and corner documented by local and visual sources.

institutionLifecycle.formation: A November 1896 fundraiser sought to establish a Lithuanian parish under a Virgin Mary title. The distinct St. Joseph parish was formally organized when Father Mykolas Vitkus was appointed on January 9, 1915.

institutionLifecycle.terminalStatus: Suppressed and merged into St. Henry Parish on April 1, 1970 according to Wolkovich's history. The current archdiocesan directory independently lists St. Joseph National Lithuanian as a closed institution with a 1915-1970 range, but does not define the exact canonical mechanism.
institutionLifecycle.currentVerification: The Archdiocese of St. Louis Archives holds the sacramental records. historicalNarrative.text: Lithuanian Catholics in St. Louis pursued a parish before St. Joseph existed. Wolkovich records a November 1896 fundraiser for an intended parish under a Virgin Mary title. That effort is a precursor milestone, not the founding date or former name of the later St. Joseph institution.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, Vol. 3, printed p. 157

historicalNarrative.text: St. Joseph was formally organized on January 9, 1915 when Father Mykolas Vitkus was appointed. The Archdiocese of St. Louis's current closed-parish directory gives the institution a 1915-1970 range and explicitly names it St. Joseph National Lithuanian, independently confirming identity, class, and closed context without defining the exact canonical erection act.

historicalNarrative.text: On August 2, 1916 the parish purchased the former Protestant Church of Unity for $9,000. St. Joseph celebrated its first Mass there on August 13, and Archbishop John Glennon blessed the church on September 10. These are property, first-worship, and blessing milestones, distinct from the 1915 institutional organization.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, Vol. 3, printed p. 158

historicalNarrative.text: The church is documented locally as 2123 Park Avenue at MacKay Place. The current archdiocesan directory instead says Park and Anderson. Because the two locators conflict, the Park Avenue street number and MacKay corner are retained from the local church list and geolocated photograph, while the official wording remains visible rather than being silently reconciled.

historicalNarrative.text: Wolkovich dates St. Joseph's suppression and merger into St. Henry Parish to April 1, 1970. The archdiocesan directory independently ends the closed institution's range in 1970 and routes its sacramental records to the Archdiocese of St. Louis Archives. The directory does not itself supply the suppression decree or merger mechanism, so the exact act rests on the historical account.

historicalNarrative.text: The former church survived the parish. A geolocated photograph taken October 5, 2023 shows the exterior standing and describes the building as rehabilitated into a single-family residence. That evidence supports standing and converted status at the photographed date, but not current occupancy, interior condition, or institutional continuity with either St. Henry or another congregation.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The 1896 Virgin Mary parish effort is a precursor, while St. Joseph was organized in 1915. The archdiocesan closed-parish directory says Park and Anderson, whereas the local church list and geolocated visual evidence place the former church at 2123 Park Avenue and MacKay Place. The directory's 1915-1970 range supports identity and closed context but does not itself define the exact erection or suppression acts.
gaps: The exact pre-1916 host worship sites; the canonical erection instrument; resolution of the Anderson-versus-MacKay location wording; the 1970 suppression and merger decree; St. Henry's precise reception of parishioners and records; any cemetery; the conversion date; and current occupancy, interior, and structural condition of the former church remain unresolved.
